the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher launches the session by displaying an actual Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) bill and a newspaper clipping regarding losses from illegal power taps on the chalkboard. The teacher challenges the 9 student teams with the prompt: 'How does paying utility bills on time and protecting public property directly transform a struggling public service into an efficient one?' Students buzz in their groups of 5-6, appointing their Spokespersons to share immediate local observations on bus delays and water wastage before transitioning into the main station rotation.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher acts as a facilitator, circulating among the 9 desk islands to distribute specialized station prompts covering railway property protection, timely utility bill settlements, and high-quality service demands. The teacher scaffolds student inquiry by asking probing questions about how vandalism on Sri Lanka Railways increases operational costs and reduces train punctuality.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students collaborate in their assigned groups of 5 or 6, assigning roles such as Scribe, Timekeeper, and Civic Investigator to analyze their specific station document. They list concrete examples of public rights and corresponding citizen duties on their draft worksheets.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Station Task Cards, Chart Paper, Colored Markers

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher monitors group progress across the room, observing how teams integrate insights from different utility sectors. The teacher intervenes with guiding prompts to help students connect citizen attitudes with overall institutional efficiency.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Group members consolidate their findings, with the Creative Director and Chart Lead organizing the information into a structured layout. They debate how positive public attitudes toward water and electricity consumption prevent wastage and ensure continuous community supply.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moderates a rapid gallery display where teams present their core conclusions. The teacher asks the Spokespersons to highlight how fulfilling specific duties directly elevates public service delivery.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Spokespersons present their group's integrated pillar chart to neighboring teams while the Civic Investigators evaluate the accuracy of the rights and duties mapped out on the displays.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Synthesized Pillar Integration Charts, Marker Pens

summary: The teacher conducts a 2-minute plenary synthesis, summarizing how balancing public rights to high-quality services with rigorous duties—such as paying bills on time and protecting property—directly drives institutional efficiency across Sri Lankan public utilities.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative evaluation is conducted by observing group collaboration, verifying the accuracy of rights and duties on the pillar charts, and assessing students' ability to articulate how individual citizen responsibility improves public sector performance.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Concept Drawing / Quick Sketch Challenge: Each student rapidly sketches a visual emblem or symbol on their notepad representing one core duty (such as paying water bills on time or protecting public bus seats) and writes a 1-sentence caption explaining how this action improves public service efficiency, evaluated immediately through peer exchange within their groups.

selected_activity:
Activity: Station Jigsaw: Mapping Rights and Responsibilities in Sri Lankan Public Utilities
Approach: Students participate in a structured station-based jigsaw rotation focusing on different pillars of public service usage: right to high quality service, duty of property protection, and economic resource consumption. Teams synthesize information across stations to build a complete picture of how reciprocal duties elevate operational efficiency in local contexts.
Student task: Teams rotate through or analyze specialized sub-topics regarding public services (e.g., railway property protection, timely utility bill payments, and demanding high-quality service responsibly), integrating their findings into a cohesive summary poster.
Teacher facilitation: The teacher sets up 3 topical focus areas across the 9 desk islands, monitors group progress every 8 minutes, and provides guiding questions on how neglecting duties harms public property and reduces service quality.
Expected output: A synthesized 'Pillar Integration Chart' illustrating the balance between public rights, duties, and institutional efficiency.
Grouping: 9 teams (4 groups of 5, 5 groups of 6) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer, Creative Director / Chart Lead. All 50 students contribute distinct perspectives according to their assigned team role.
